verdict.rationale: First-party docs cover both halves of the story. For synthetic data, Isaac Sim's Replicator generates labeled training data, and Isaac Sim supports controllable synthetic data pipelines and randomized scene capture. For reinforcement learning, Isaac Lab is a GPU-accelerated framework for training robot policies at scale: it supports RL and imitation learning, integrates skrl, RLLib and rl_games, and runs headless from workstation to data center. The community sim-to-real drift report concerns how simulations transfer to real hardware, not whether data generation or RL training works, so it does not create a dispute. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of large-scale training and data generation, and concrete scale or throughput figures.
